summary: Deeply nested structured-output causes long-tail decode latency and intermittent request timeouts (streaming JSON mode)
description: Customer DataWave reports intermittent 10-30s tail latencies and occasional request timeouts when using streaming JSON/structured-output mode against our hosted API. Issue appears only for prompts that request deeply nested arrays/objects (e.g., multi-level tokenization outputs, nested 'chunks' arrays). The problem is surfaced as: (a) streaming connection remains open but no 'complete' event is emitted, causing client timeouts, and (b) individual requests occasionally hit the platform timeout (upstream 30s) with serving-runtime showing high decode CPU and GC spikes. Impact: Several production features at DataWave are degraded; they are on an enterprise contract and report customer-facing outages.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a request with streaming=true and output_format=json (structured mode).
2) Prompt that requests nested arrays, example: 'Return analysis as {"batches": [ {"chunks": [ {"tokens": [ ...nested 7-10 levels... ] } ] } ] }'.
3) Use max_tokens=1024, temperature=0.0, and chunk_size=256, with client set to 30s request timeout.
4) Send 50 parallel requests from us-west; observe percent of requests finishing vs timing out and tail latency distribution.
Expected: streaming incremental JSON chunks arrive and finalization within SLO (<2s median for small responses, <1s tail increase).
Observed: many requests show steady streaming then stall for 8-30s while server CPU and memory allocation spike; some requests time out without final JSON close token.

comments: Support - Riley Chen (2026-03-12): Opened after receiving multiple escalations from DataWave CSM. Customer provides sample payloads; they can reproduce locally against our hosted endpoint.
Customer - DataWave (2026-03-12): 'We see 15% request timeouts when processing nested token arrays. Non-streaming JSON mode returns slowly but completes; streaming seems to hang.'

Eng - Miguel Torres (2026-03-12): Confirmed reproduction in staging with the sample prompt. Profiling shows long pauses in the JSON incremental decoder and large temporary buffers created when encountering deep nesting. Assigned SRE to monitor memory churn.

SRE - Aisha Patel (2026-03-13): Grafana: rx latency p95 jumped from 1.1s -> 7.6s for affected route; correlates with increased allocator churn on nodes running the streaming decoder. Investigating potential pathological recursion or iterative parsing fallback.
Support - Riley Chen (2026-03-13): Provided temporary client workaround: set stream=false or request flattened output to avoid deep nesting. Customer asks for ETA to full fix.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: streaming incremental parser accumulates buffer per top-level array but does not flush partial objects when deeply nested arrays are present; causes O(n^2) reserialization in worst case.
Reproduced in staging: increasing explicit nesting depth from 3 to 9 increases decode CPU ~linearly and increases GC pauses superlinearly (observed 3x GC time at depth 9).
Heap profile indicates many short-lived allocations during decoder's 'emit_chunk' path; copy-on-emit creates transient strings repeatedly when nested containers are closed.
Observed a lock contention on streaming write queue on nodes with high load; decoder backpressure not applied early enough, causing upstream batching to grow.
Quick local patch: avoid full serialization on partial emits and switch to incremental token emission reduces tail latency in reproducible test by ~60%.
Related prior ticket SUP-7021 shows schema validation path can also add latency when combined with nesting — possible compound effect.
resolution: Workaround: customer advised to use stream=false or request flattened JSON until fix is deployed. Mitigation: deployed hotfix to staging that reduces transient allocations in streaming decoder; fix PR is under review (runtime PR #1984). Next steps: run canary, validate with DataWave test payloads, and schedule rollout to prod-us-west. No full prod rollout yet; ETA for rollout 2026-03-18 pending canary results.
next_steps: 1) Complete PR review and run 24h canary in prod-us-west with traffic mirror of 5% (owner: Miguel Torres).
2) Add additional unit tests targeting deep nesting and large array streaming to prevent regressions (owner: Runtime team).
3) Update client docs to recommend flattened outputs for streaming heavy nested data and document known limitation until fixed.
4) Post-mortem if rollout required more than two attempts; include memory allocation and decoder design notes.
